_comment: EXP-30 ablation. The mix cycles and the rate does NOT: 40 req/s flat for nine
minutes, m1 -> m2 -> m3 -> m1 on two-minute segments.
It exists to separate the two things mix_dyn60_short_m123.json varies together.
40 req/s is the lowest rate at which the fixed-rate sweep separated the
policies at all (PolyServe 54.4% against FluidServe 100.0%), so any difference
here is attributable to the mix moving rather than to the load level.
Two-minute segments rather than fifteen: PolyServe's partition adapts in about
30 s (10 s window, EWMA alpha 0.5, two agreeing rounds before it acts), so a
two-minute segment leaves the transient as roughly a quarter of the segment
instead of a thirtieth. This is the most favourable timing for the claim that
a static partition mistracks, and is labelled as such: if no difference shows
up even here, the claim does not hold on this workload at any timescale a real
